data.body:
Root cause PROVEN and fix LANDED as 7c763f1a7 (Gerrit change 993, LLM-Review +1 / Verified +1, MERGED).

PROOF OF MECHANISM (clean sandbox: real bare "remote" + working clone, real _ref_lock primitives, no mocks)
Sequence reproduced exactly, requiring NO crash or interruption:
  acquire(remote='origin', holder='GHA-bridge')  -> local=(absent)     remote=bcb5352334
  read(remote='origin')                          -> local=bcb5352334   remote=bcb5352334   <- local COPY PLANTED by _fetch_ref
  release(oid, remote='origin')                  -> local=bcb5352334   remote=(absent)     <- STRANDED: remote-only delete
  read(remote='origin')                          -> HELD holder=GHA-bridge                 <- but remote is FREE
  steal(sleep_fn=noop)                           -> None                                   <- CANNOT break it
Net: wedged permanently; manual `git update-ref -d` the only escape.

Also measured directly: running the exact command _fetch_ref issues, `git fetch origin +refs/reconciler/lock:refs/reconciler/lock`, against an absent remote ref fails with `fatal: couldn't find remote ref refs/reconciler/lock` (exit 128) and the stale LOCAL ref SURVIVES unchanged — falsifying the old comment at _ref_lock.py:290-292 which claimed it "becomes absent locally = free".

AUTHORITY (why this is a defect, not a misconfiguration)
docs/adr/0031-reconciler-ref-lock.md §"Distributed operation": "The lock must be authoritative across CI runners, manual invocations, and clones"; with remote="origin" "the remote is the truth". A stranded local ref overriding a free remote violates that directly.
Same ADR §"Operator break-glass": "C2's relative-duration lease makes this rarely necessary — a crashed holder's lock becomes steal-able after one lease interval automatically." Here it was NEVER steal-able and break-glass was ALWAYS required. The ADR names both halves of a clear (`git push origin :refs/reconciler/lock` AND `git update-ref -d refs/reconciler/lock`), so the design knows the local ref is a separate artifact release must handle.

RULED OUT
- Steal kill-switch: REBAR_RECONCILER_LOCK_STEAL defaults ON (__main__.py:170-184), unset locally; driving steal_pass_lock directly DID break a stale lease (fence 2 -> 3). Stealing was never disabled.
- Hidden local pass source (the user's "bridge should be GitHub-Actions-only" concern): no git hook, LaunchAgent (only com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update, a pipx build updater, and rebar-worktree-gc — neither references reconcile), crontab, MCP tool, or implicit CLI path runs a pass. The only reconcile entry is the explicit `rebar reconcile` intercept. Operator-run local passes plus THIS bug fully explain recurrence.
- _advisory_lock's fail-closed swallow: no exception is raised; steal() returns None cleanly.

CORRECTED EARLIER OBSERVATION
An initial `git ls-remote origin 'refs/reconciler/*'` returned empty, which I first read as "the GHA bridge holds no lock". That was a brief inter-pass window: repeated polling returns a DIFFERENT oid each sample (e6674ba4…, 75e3bc20…), i.e. the bridge holds and heartbeats the remote lock near-continuously. This strengthens the diagnosis — nearly any local read plants an orphan.

TEST (RED->GREEN, held out from the fixer)
tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_lock_orphan_local_ref.py — 5 tests driving real git repos through the real primitives. Confirmed RED first (4 failed for the right reasons: read reports HELD against a free remote; release leaves the local ref; the orphan is unbreakable; a pre-existing orphan is not pruned), then GREEN 5/5 against a fix the implementing subagent never saw.
Mutation checks, one per half of the fix: neutering the release-side local delete -> RED (test_release_in_remote_mode_leaves_no_local_ref); neutering the fetch-side prune -> RED (test_preexisting_orphan_is_pruned_on_read). The first oracle version MISSED the second mutation, so it was strengthened with the production-shape case (bridge releases on its own runner, so no local release ever cleans the ref) — the fix was reverted first, the revised test re-verified RED, then the fix restored, per RED-before-GREEN discipline.
Guard against the opposite failure: test_a_genuinely_held_remote_lock_is_still_respected passed throughout — a live remote holder still reads HELD, so cross-machine mutual exclusion is preserved.

SAFETY VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY
An UNREACHABLE remote (origin url repointed at a nonexistent path, local orphan present) still reads HELD — fail-closed. A network outage cannot make every lock look free. Discriminator is `git ls-remote --exit-code` EXIT STATUS (0 present / 2 reachable-but-absent / else unknown), which is locale-independent, rather than matching git's stderr text.

REPLICATION ON THE LIVE CHECKOUT
During a genuine inter-pass window (remote FREE, local orphan 0d18075c3e present), read(root, LOCK_REF, remote='origin') logged
  INFO: ref-lock: pruning orphaned local refs/reconciler/lock — remote origin is reachable and the ref is absent
returned FREE, and the local ref is now absent. Before the fix this same state returned HELD forever.
(Note: an earlier `rebar reconcile --mode reconcile-check` run I cited proved less than claimed — the remote ref was present at the time and reconcile-check does not take the pass lock. The inter-pass-window test above is the real replication.)

GATES
Gerrit 993: LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, MERGED as 7c763f1a7. tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/ 1438 passed. make lint clean; make typecheck "Success: no issues found in 381 source files". _ref_lock.py 765 LOC (under the 800 cap). Caller sweep: _fetch_ref has ONE caller (_ref_oid) and release ONE (_advisory_lock) — no behavioural dependency on the old behaviour; no existing test was modified or weakened.
